content.text: Knowledge confirms Canvas Workspace with an explicit note that keyboard alternatives are required — exactly the acceptance seed. Recording the decision.

avoid: dialogs or forms that mediate placement semantics
edge-per-relationship clutter; proximity shown only for the selection
strategy: canvas dominant, quiet chrome (P-22)
zone tints + labeled chips carry grouping before detail is read (P-01)
detail only on selection via contextual inspector (H-19)
counts and status hints instead of extra panels (P-26)

primary: Floor canvas with zones and placed objects (dominant surface)
Selection-driven inspector showing derived facts: zone (from position), coordinates, nearest neighbor + distance
Zone rail: named zones with live occupancy counts and send-to hotkeys 1..n
secondary: Status bar: landing hint during placement/drag, cursor coords, zoom, snap state
Keyboard help overlay on demand (?), closed by default

major_choices.choice: Keyboard-first creation via ghost-placing mode: N (object) / R (region) spawns a ghost that arrow-keys position (Shift = coarse), Enter commits, Esc cancels; double-click creates in place
major_choices.rationale: Makes create verb keyboard-native, satisfying 落位即意图 without pointer dependency

major_choices.choice: Derived-only semantics: zone membership = object center containment; neighbor = nearest center distance; no assignment metadata exists to edit
major_choices.rationale: Position is the single source of truth, so moving always re-derives meaning — placement is intent by construction

major_choices.choice: Send-to-zone hotkeys 1..n teleport the selected object into the first free grid slot of that zone
major_choices.rationale: Keyboard equivalent of dragging a token into a zone; pairs with arrows for fine placement

major_choices.choice: Landing hint: during placing/dragging, status bar names the zone under the object and the zone border highlights (P-26)
major_choices.rationale: Closes the action loop: users see the intent consequence before committing

major_choices.choice: Light localStorage autosave with visible Reset Scene; persistence is a courtesy, not a service
major_choices.rationale: Product feel without violating 'no persistence service required' constraint

rejected.reason: does_not_apply_when spatial relationships dominate; collection order is meaningless here

rejected.option: Table/grid of object records as primary
rejected.reason: Forces position into cells, destroying placement-is-intent
The space is an abstract physical floor, not georeferenced

primary.reason: Spatial continuity on a physical floor is the product object itself; canvas is the only representation where position carries meaning natively

supporting.reason: Zone rail listing zones with occupancy counts and send-to hotkeys keeps the many-object population legible

# Plotboard — 落位即意图 · placement is intent

A single-page **spatial workspace**: a floor canvas with named zones, where you create
labeled objects and *land* them. Where an object sits **is** what it means — zone
membership is pure containment, "nearest" is pure center distance. Nothing is assigned
through forms; moving an object re-derives its meaning instantly.

Cell: `cell-j07-s07` (create × spatial-workspace) · acceptance seed: **空间操作有键盘等价物**
— every spatial operation has a keyboard equivalent.

## Run

No build, no backend, no external services.

- Open `index.html` directly (`file://` works), or
- serve the folder statically (e.g. `python -m http.server`) and open `/`.

The page renders a populated demo floor (4 zones, 13 tiles) synchronously at first
paint — there is no loading state. Scene changes autosave to `localStorage`;
**Reset scene** (two-click confirm) restores the built-in demo.

## Keyboard map (the acceptance seed)

| Group | Keys |
|---|---|
| Create & place | `N` new object · `R` new zone · `↑↓←→` position ghost (`Shift` ×5) · `Enter` drop · `Esc` cancel · double-click create/rename in place |
| Select | `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` cycle tiles · click select · `Ctrl+A` select all · `Esc` deselect |
| Move & place | `↑↓←→` nudge (`Shift` ×5; pans when nothing selected) · `1`–`8` send selection to zone n · drag to move · `[` `]` z-order |
| View | `W A S D` pan · `+` `−` zoom · `0` fit · `F` focus selection · wheel zoom · `Space`+drag pan |
| Edit | `Ctrl+D` duplicate · `Del` delete (deleting a zone keeps its tiles) · `G` snap toggle · `Enter` rename |
| Help | `?` keyboard map overlay |

Every pointer spatial operation (create, place, move, send-to-zone, pan, zoom) has the
keyboard equivalent listed above; press `?` in the app for the live overlay.

## Product logic

- **Zones (regions)** are named rectangles. A tile's zone = the zone containing its
  center point, recomputed on every move. Tile color dot + rail counts + inspector
  facts are all *derived* — there is no assignment metadata anywhere in the model.
- **Landing preview**: while placing or dragging, the status bar names the zone the
  object would land in and the zone border highlights (落位 → …).
- **Derived relation**: selecting a tile draws its nearest-neighbor link with distance
  in grid units and lists the fact in the inspector.

## Files

```
index.html   markup: titlebar · zone rail · floor canvas · inspector · status bar · help overlay
styles.css   design tokens + all styling (dark floor-canvas theme)
app.js       state, persistence (localStorage), view transform, pointer + keyboard interactions
```

Vanilla ES2017, zero dependencies, works from `file://`.

# Deliverable: **Plotboard** — 落位即意图 · placement is intent

A single-page spatial workspace for `cell-j07-s07` (create × spatial-workspace). You create labeled objects and *land* them on a floor with named zones. **Where an object sits IS what it means**: zone membership = center containment, "nearest" = center distance — recomputed on every move, never stored as metadata. Every spatial operation has a keyboard equivalent (the acceptance seed): `N`/`R` ghost-placing → arrows → `Enter`, `1`–`8` send-to-zone, arrows nudge/pan, `Tab` cycle, `WASD` pan, `+`/`−`/`0`/`F` view, `Ctrl+D`, `[`/`]`, `G`, `?` help overlay — with pointer drag/wheel as the parallel input.

## Files (all new, zero dependencies)
- `index.html` — titlebar · zone rail · floor canvas · inspector · status bar · help overlay
- `styles.css` — dark floor-canvas theme, tokens, AA-contrast focus states
- `app.js` — state, derived semantics, view transform, pointer + full keyboard shadow, localStorage autosave + two-step Reset
- `README.md`, `tools/shot.js` + `package.json` (evidence harness, not part of the app)

**Run:** open `index.html` directly (`file://` works — classic scripts, no build). First paint renders the inlined demo scene (4 zones, 13 tiles) synchronously — ready state, no loading state.

## Prax trail (session `ds_20260918221722_0377b4fb`)
All gates executed and passed: requirement confirmation → frame → context → route (Canvas Workspace pattern, whose contract itself demands "keyboard and list alternatives") → inspect → decide (2 lint iterations: exact `dominant_workspace` token + object-id references required) → sdir → reconcile (1 explicit compromise: no undo/redo) → realize (direct_code) → prepare_implementation → validate. **Final phase: VALIDATION / WARN** — 8 deterministic checks measured-pass; `requirement_alignment`, `product_model_alignment`, `state_completeness`, `destructive_recovery` pass (attested); 5 visual/empirical checks honestly `inconclusive`.

## Evidence status — reported plainly
**No screenshots could be captured in this harness.** I verified every execution route before concluding: no shell tool exists (full registry dump), the chrome MCP server isn't connected (`select:` verified), the browser-user agent had no `use_browser` binding, the general-purpose agent shares the same restricted set, and the Codex agent refuses with zero tools. I did **not** fabricate captures. A complete CDP harness is ready — on any machine with Node + Edge/Chrome:
```
npm install && node tools\shot.js
```
It drives the full keyboard journey (Tab-inspect → N→arrows→Enter → send-to-zone → help → zone-delete-keeps-tiles → reload-autosave → reset) and writes 9 annotated screenshots + a JSON assertion report into `evidence/`, which can then be submitted via `design_validate submit_evidence` to flip the 5 pending checks.

## Budget (within caps)
- **Tokens:** ~140k of 1.2M
- **Wall-clock:** ~75 min of 90 (per Prax server timestamps 22:17Z → 23:3xZ)

One recorded deviation: the `design_prepare_implementation` schema forces `framework: react`; the implementation is deliberately framework-free vanilla ES2017 to guarantee static `file://` open with zero build — noted in the gate's measurement target and in the submitted validation evidence.
